findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py post_evidence: it loops over _evidence_records(...) looking for the dedupe_key, then calls _gh(... POST comments) unconditionally. Readers (requirement_evidence) do not collapse duplicates by dedupe_key or event_id, so duplicate durable events could be counted twice in a Requirement retrospective.
findings.summary: post_evidence dedupes by reading existing records and then posting, with no atomicity, so concurrent coordinator runs can write duplicate evidence comments for one dedupe key.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py _touches_openspec_change: run_git(['merge-base', head, 'origin/main']) followed by git diff --name-only base...head. The function does not fetch, and it does not compare against the PR's actual base. Design D4 accepts the safe-direction failure, but a stale local ref still makes admission outcomes depend on local fetch freshness.
findings.summary: The managed-candidate predicate in _touches_openspec_change diffs against the local origin/main ref, which may be stale. A stale ref can misclassify a quick task as managed (a safe failure) or produce a spurious merge-base error.
